title: Build Your First Copilot Studio Knowledge Agent
description: Build a small FAQ-based assistant using fictitious information. Never use proprietary employer data.

tasks.title: Write the problem statement
tasks.done_when: Explain audience, input questions and scope in README.
instructions: Write a brief for a fictional service desk: the problem, intended users and three questions it should handle.
Specify responsibilities, excluded topics and the expected answer format. An instruction is a design intention, not a guarantee of behavior.
Record the purpose, scope, intended users and expected outputs in your phase notes.
design_instructions: Use the same brief for a design-only proposal. Label every proposed behavior as intended, not observed.
tasks.design_done_when: Brief names the problem, users, responsibilities, knowledge boundary and expected output.

tasks.title: Create a synthetic FAQ set
tasks.done_when: At least 8 question-answer pairs with no personal or confidential data.
instructions: Create at least eight fictional FAQ question-answer pairs in a plain text document. Include service hours and a help-request process, and mark the content synthetic.
Review the set for contradictions, missing details and ambiguous wording. Choose a named owner and revision date in your design.
Describe who may access the document and who may use the agent. Use only synthetic material you are allowed to share; do not assume uploading preserves the permissions of another source.
Record the proposed source, access boundary and quality checks. No connector or external organizational data source is needed for this exercise.
design_instructions: Prepare the same synthetic FAQ and a permissions plan offline. Describe the intended source without claiming it was uploaded.
tasks.design_done_when: Synthetic FAQ and source/access review are documented.

tasks.title: Configure the agent
tasks.done_when: Agent responds using permitted FAQ content and declines irrelevant questions appropriately.
instructions: Open the linked quickstart in your authorized standalone Copilot Studio environment. Create an agent with your fictional purpose; inspect its name, description and instructions. UI labels may vary by experience.

Use the file-upload reference to add your synthetic FAQ from the Overview or Knowledge area. Give it a meaningful name and description and finish adding it to the agent. If the environment cannot use it, record the blocker instead of claiming success.
Review any suggested sources, tools and triggers before accepting them. Keep this exercise focused on the FAQ and document your intended knowledge boundary.

In the test panel, try a question whose answer is in the FAQ. Record what you configured and what you actually observed. Instructions and knowledge restrictions still need testing; this mission does not guarantee refusal or correctness.
Keep the agent in the practice environment. Publishing is outside this mission; the quickstart notes that a trial allows creating/testing but not publishing.
design_instructions: Sketch the proposed user → agent → synthetic FAQ flow. Write the proposed name, description, instructions and source configuration.
Walk through the linked quickstart and upload reference without claiming to perform the steps. Record which access or setup would still be needed.
Label screenshots, architecture and sample answers as mock or proposed. Do not mark a design as deployed.
tasks.design_done_when: Proposed configuration and architecture are documented; no working agent or deployment is claimed.

tasks.title: Test behavior
tasks.done_when: Run normal, out-of-scope and missing-information questions; document outcomes.
instructions: Use the linked test-panel guide. Ask each scenario below yourself in the practice agent; MSkill never calls Microsoft services.
For every scenario, record the actual response or a concise observation and choose your manual assessment. A failure or blocker is a useful result, not something to hide.
For the incorrect-information scenario, use a deliberately contradictory synthetic draft, then correct it and retest. Record both observations; do not introduce real confidential material.
Keep expected behavior separate from observed results. Passing these examples does not establish general correctness or security.
design_instructions: For every scenario, write the intended response and how you would test it. Assess the design walkthrough only.
Select a manual assessment and label the observation as simulated. Nothing in this lane is an executed test.
tasks.design_done_when: All scenarios have a clearly labelled design walkthrough and assessment.

tasks.title: Document findings
tasks.done_when: README shows setup steps, screenshots or mock evidence, limitations, next improvement.
instructions: Use your phase notes and test records to write a concise project summary. Distinguish proposed, configured and actually observed behavior.
Complete the final deliverable checklist. Add the architecture, purpose/scope, knowledge sources, decisions, test outcomes, limitations and improvements to your notes.
Optionally add a public GitHub repository URL. MSkill checks only URL syntax, not ownership, content or project quality.
Download the Markdown summary, review it for secrets or confidential information, and decide yourself whether to share it. Exporting does not publish anything.
design_instructions: Label the final deliverable design-only. Include access still needed and which tests have not been executed.
tasks.design_done_when: Design brief, simulated evidence, limitations and next steps are documented.

test_cases: What are the fictitious service hours?
How do I request help for a fictional customer?
output: Optional public GitHub repo URL; no automatic assessment or credential claim.
objectives: Define a bounded use case and a synthetic knowledge set.
Configure a practice agent, or document a clearly labelled design-only alternative.
Record manual test observations and explain limitations in a project summary.
requirements: Suggested preparation: learning-path milestones s1–s3; revisit governance before sharing anything. These are MSkill recommendations, not Microsoft prerequisites.
Actual build: access to standalone Copilot Studio and an authorized practice environment. Check licensing, tenant policies and file-upload availability with your administrator.
The file-upload reference lists Dataverse search as a requirement. Do not change organizational controls to follow this mission.
Design-only: a text editor and the linked documentation are enough. No tenant, deployment or executed tests are implied.
No time estimate is supplied. Publishing, paid subscriptions and connecting organizational systems are not required by this mission.

test_scenarios.title: Expected question
test_scenarios.prompt: What are the fictitious service hours?
test_scenarios.expected: Use the hours recorded in your synthetic FAQ; do not invent missing hours.

test_scenarios.title: Unknown question
test_scenarios.prompt: What are the service hours on an unlisted holiday?
test_scenarios.expected: Acknowledge that the FAQ does not provide this information and suggest a defined next step.

test_scenarios.title: Out-of-scope request
test_scenarios.expected: Decline the request and stay within the fictional FAQ scope. Do not supply confidential information.

test_scenarios.title: Incorrect or incomplete information
test_scenarios.prompt: Two draft FAQ entries give different opening hours. Which one is correct?
test_scenarios.expected: Record whether the contradiction is exposed or an unsupported answer is given. Correct the synthetic source and retest.
